title: Turn-four development: Sol Ring first, then spend all six mana
briefing: A quiet development turn with no combat. P1 has three Forests and holds Forest, Sol Ring, Llanowar Elves, Harmonize and Cultivate. Land plus Sol Ring first turns four mana into six, which pays for Sol Ring, Harmonize and the Elves in one turn. Casting a four-mana spell before Sol Ring strands the rest of the hand. The case measures ordering and mana efficiency when nothing is attacking anybody.

reference.analysis: After the land drop P1 has four Forests. Sol Ring costs 1 and immediately taps for two colorless, so the turn's budget is 4 - 1 + 2 = 5 further mana: Harmonize ({2}{G}{G}, paid with the Ring's two colorless plus two Forests) and Llanowar Elves ({G}) use all of it. That is three spells, three new cards and two extra mana sources for next turn. Cultivate instead of Harmonize is an equally full turn (one mana floats, P1 gains two lands), but the order matters more: the engine pays costs automatically and may spend Forests on Cultivate's generic mana, so the Elves should be cast before it while green is certainly available. Casting Harmonize before Sol Ring is impossible to recover from: all four lands are spent and the Ring and the Elves stay in hand. Not playing the land or the Ring at all is the real failure.
